Humanoids

UBTECH and FAW-Volkswagen extend humanoid work into factory logistics

The agreement covers joint development, testing and demonstration scenarios, building on earlier quality-inspection training in Qingdao.

Pandaily ↗8 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A broader agreement

UBTECH announced an agreement with FAW-Volkswagen on October 8 to develop and test embodied robots for logistics and establish demonstration scenarios. The new development is the formal expansion in scope. The relationship began in 2024, so earlier trials should not be presented as newly launched deployments.

Building on inspection work

Walker S Lite previously trained on vehicle quality inspection at the Qingdao plant, integrating with factory automation. Logistics extends the focus toward material handling. UBTECH describes a stack spanning decision-making, motion control, robot hardware and multi-robot coordination, with foundation, world and action models supporting perception and behavior.

Operational results are still needed

The agreement reports no robot quantity, contract value, complete rollout schedule or task-success rate. Demonstration scenarios are a step toward evaluation, rather than evidence of humanoid deployment throughout every FAW-Volkswagen factory. The next useful evidence will concern performance within actual material flows.
